summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and esophagitis was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by poor oral intake and vomiting. She was treated in the ICU with an insulin drip, which was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin as her anion gap closed and blood sugars stabilized. Nausea and vomiting improved with antiemetics, and she advanced to a soft diet. A possible UTI was ruled out due to urine contamination, and antibiotics were discontinued. Her home antihypertensives were restarted, and she was switched to pantoprazole for esophagitis. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue her insulin regimen, take pantoprazole daily, and follow up with endocrinology and gastroenterology.
